title: ChatGPT for Good? On Opportunities and Challenges of Large Language Models for Education
extended_summary:
This position paper examines the opportunities and risks of large language models, especially ChatGPT, for education. Rather than reporting an empirical intervention study, it synthesizes early uses of LLMs in educational settings and argues for responsible, human-centered deployment. The paper asks how such models can support learning and teaching, and what technical, pedagogical, ethical, legal, and social challenges must be addressed before they can be used at scale.

The authors discuss a wide range of possible applications for students and teachers, including generating quizzes, practice problems, explanations, personalized feedback, lesson plans, summaries, and assessment support. The discussion spans multiple educational levels and contexts, with examples relevant to elementary through university learners, as well as group, remote, and professional learning. Particular attention is given to potential uses in middle and high school education, such as language learning, mathematics practice, and problem-solving support.

The paper concludes that LLMs may become powerful educational tools, but only if they are integrated with strong human oversight, critical thinking, fact-checking, privacy protections, bias mitigation, and sustainable governance. It emphasizes that these systems should supplement rather than replace teachers, and it calls for more research on best practices, user interfaces, fairness, and reliable educational use cases.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a position paper and narrative overview, not an empirical evaluation with a controlled design. It presents arguments, use cases, and risks without original outcome data.
impact_tier_rationale: No direct learning or implementation effect is measured, so there is no empirical evidence of impact on outcomes in this paper.

interventions.use_case: Position paper on ChatGPT and other large language models as educational assistants for students and teachers, including conversational tutoring, question answering, personalized explanations, and generation of practice problems, quizzes, and feedback.
